newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister sees inflation rise followed by fall.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister sees inflation rise followed by fall.

text.p: Turkish State Minister Gunes Taner, responsible for the economy in the new government, said on Monday he expected a near-term rise in the country's chronic inflation to be followed by a rapid decline.
"Inflation will rise somewhat and then fall quickly," Taner told a news conference. Wholesale price inflation was up 75.7 percent annually in June, a slight rise from the previous month.
Taner was speaking after the announcement of 15-32 percent petroleum product price rises. Consumption taxes on petroleum products were increased by between 20 and 90 percentage points.
"This adjustment was felt to be necessary and important from the view of establishing the general balances of the economy," he said.
"Such price adjustments will have a chain effect in the next three-four months," he added.
Taner said the two-week-old government had decided to adjust prices as a way of raising resources rather than increasing taxes.
"If we had not adjusted the petroleum prices, inflation in 1998 would have risen to greater dimensions or even come to the point of exploding," he said.
The new minister said the right-left coalition, which took over from an Islamist-led government, would avoid populist measures.
